import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Prime Triplet Conjecture

*Reference:* [Prime Triplet Wikipedia Page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_triplet#Conjecture_on_prime_triplets)
-/

namespace PrimeTriplets

/--
Are there infinitely many tuples of three consecutive primes $(p, q, r)$ such that $r - p = 6$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem prime_triplets :
    answer(sorry) ↔ {p : ℕ | Prime p ∧ (Prime (p + 2) ∨ Prime (p + 4)) ∧ Prime (p + 6)}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end PrimeTriplets

reformulations.difference: Lean asserts infinitude of starting primes satisfying either offset pattern, rather than explicitly asserting infinitude of triples of consecutive primes whose largest and smallest elements differ by six.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Primality of p and p+6 forces p ≥ 5. Any prime strictly between them must, by parity, be p+2 or p+4. Both cannot be prime: one of p, p+2, p+4 is divisible by 3, and all exceed 3. Thus each qualifying p determines exactly one consecutive-prime triple. Conversely, every increasing prime triple of span six has one of these patterns. Projection to the smallest prime is therefore a bijection and preserves infinitude. Wikipedia conjectures infinitude of the combined family, so the disjunction is appropriate. Both the span-six and consecutive-triple infinitude equivalences were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.
